questions.topic: The Else Block On A Try
questions.learningObjective: Predict when the else block runs
questions.stem: In the study group, a try block succeeds and an else follows; does the else block run?

options.text: Yes, because else runs when no exception occurs
No, because else only runs after an exception
No, because else is unreachable after success
Yes, but only if finally is present

questions.explanation: The else block runs only when the try completes without an exception. Option B confuses else with except; option C thinks success skips it; option D conditions on finally.
questions.hint: else runs on the clean path.

questions.topic: The Cleanup Block On A Clean Path
questions.learningObjective: Predict whether finally runs on success
questions.stem: The study group asks whether finally runs when the try succeeds; what is the answer?

options.text: Yes, finally always runs
No, finally only runs after an exception
No, finally only runs if except is present
Yes, but only if else is absent

questions.explanation: finally runs regardless of whether an exception occurred. Option B limits it to exceptions; option C conditions on except; option D conditions on else.

questions.learningObjective: Explain what finally guarantees
questions.stem: The study group asks what finally guarantees in a try/except/finally; name the guarantee.

options.text: It runs on both success and failure paths
It runs only on failure
It runs only on success
It runs only if no handler matched

questions.explanation: finally runs whether the try succeeded, raised a caught exception, or raised an uncaught one. Option B limits to failure; option C to success; option D to handler miss.

questions.learningObjective: Predict what happens when finally raises
questions.stem: The study group asks what happens when finally raises an exception; write a model answer.

answer.exemplar: If finally raises, its exception replaces any in-flight exception and propagates, potentially masking the original error.

questions.explanation: The exemplar explains that finally's exception replaces and masks the original. It is accurate and concise.

questions.learningObjective: Predict the type of a custom exception instance
questions.stem: How many base classes does a minimal custom exception class need to declare?
questions.explanation: A custom exception typically subclasses Exception alone, one base class. Declaring more is optional.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the correct base for a custom exception
questions.stem: In the study group, a student defines class MyError: pass without a base; what is the risk?

options.text: It subclasses object, not Exception, so except Exception misses it
It subclasses Exception automatically
It becomes abstract and unraisable
It raises SyntaxError

questions.explanation: A class with no base subclasses object, so it is not an Exception and except Exception does not catch it. Option B assumes implicit base; option C thinks abstract; option D expects syntax error.
questions.hint: No base means object, not Exception.

questions.learningObjective: Predict when an assertion error occurs

Nothing, because assert is a no-op
It prints a warning only
The expression is evaluated but ignored

questions.topic: The Else Block On A Try

questions.learningObjective: Explain why subclassing Exception is correct
questions.stem: The study group asks why custom exceptions should subclass Exception; write a model answer.

answer.exemplar: Subclassing Exception makes the custom error catchable by except Exception and keeps it out of the BaseException control-flow exceptions.

questions.explanation: The exemplar explains catchability by except Exception and separation from control exceptions. It is accurate and concise.

questions.explanation: Exception stores the argument, so str(exc) is 'oops'. Option B thinks ignored; option C confuses name; option D thinks __init__ required.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why finally is used for resource cleanup

questions.learningObjective: Predict whether a custom exception carries args
questions.stem: If a custom exception is raised with two arguments, how many items are in exc.args?
questions.explanation: Exception stores all positional arguments in args, so two arguments yield two items. This holds for custom subclasses too.

questions.learningObjective: Explain how to add custom data to an exception

questions.explanation: The exemplar explains overriding __init__ and calling super().__init__() to preserve message and args. It is accurate and concise.

questions.topic: The Else Block On A Try
